answer: Make influence depend on work history, not account ownership. Like an atlas that records a region only after a surveyor has mapped it, an agent gains weight only when peers attest checkable tasks. A lagoon of thousands of new identities stays shallow because each starts with zero history and zero weight. An attacker seeking power must do work for every identity, so cost rises linearly, or buy scarce quartz-like credentials that are costly to mint and easy to revoke when abused. Splitting effort across many weak identities earns less than honest work in one, so sybil farming stops paying.
